evidence.observation: The only slug implementation used by the contract demo (imported, not copied). It is a pure character scanner: CJK runs (㐀-䶿一-鿿豈-﫿) are preserved verbatim (L46-50), latin/digit runs are lowercased (L51-54), every other character (space, punctuation) closes the current segment (L55-58), and the segments are joined with '-' with repeated/leading/trailing hyphens collapsed (L63). Task-relevant behavior: on the contracted docs/agents corpus this maps 'Redis 主从' -> 'redis-主从', 'redis-主从!' -> 'redis-主从' (so two different raw titles collide deterministically), '1. 客户端接入配置' -> '1-客户端接入配置' and 'TDAI v2 — Technical Ops Guide (for Nick)' -> 'tdai-v2-technical-ops-guide-for-nick'. Because it is a pure function, identical titles always produce identical slugs; the demo proves idempotence (slugify(slugify(x)) === slugify(x)) over 27 corpus-derived probes and uses the result as the dedup key for pages and the base for heading anchors.

Maps a declared page type to its wiki directory through the TYPE_DIR table (source->sources, entity->entities, concept/methodology->concepts, ...), lowercasing the lookup key and falling back to the lowercased type itself for unregistered types (L86). Task-relevant behavior: in the corpus 'entity' lands pages in wiki/entities/, 'source' in wiki/sources/, the unregistered 'assets' in wiki/assets/, and every malformed-frontmatter page falls back to type 'other' -> wiki/other/. The fallback directory is therefore itself deterministic and never empty ('other' when the key is blank).

Composes the canonical dedup key 'wiki/<dir>/<slug>.md' from (type, title) using slugify() and dirForType(). This is the key the demo uses to detect cross-file collisions: the corpus files entity-redis-2.md (title 'redis-主从!') and entity-redis.md (title 'Redis 主从') both request wiki/entities/redis-主从.md, which is emitted as PAGE_PATH_COLLISION and resolved deterministically by code-point file order (first keeps the requested path, second moves to wiki/entities/redis-主从-2.md). This mirrors the type+title branch of canonicalizePagePath() in MemoryKnowledge/src/engines/wiki/ingest-v2/index.ts:392-411, which feeds the same helper into the ingest dedup path.

Defines the tolerant frontmatter contract that the demo's invalid-metadata handling mirrors: if the '---' block is missing the reader returns {type:'other'} with hasFrontmatter:false (L45-47); if YAML parsing throws it returns the same fallback while keeping the body (L51-55); a parsed non-object yields the same fallback (L56-58); and only a non-empty string type survives, everything else collapsing to 'other' (L60). Task-relevant behavior: the corpus contains an unterminated block, an invalid flow sequence, a duplicate key and a non-mapping root, and each is expected to degrade to type 'other' instead of throwing or aborting ingestion. The demo keeps those semantics but adds an explicit diagnostic per rejected block, because the library's fallback is silent.

Reads the page's declared sources and keeps only string entries, returning [] for anything that is not an array. Task-relevant behavior: the corpus page agent-codebuddy.md declares 'sources: [raw/agents/codebuddy.md, 42, null, true]'; the contract normalizes it to exactly ['raw/agents/codebuddy.md'] and records FM_SOURCES_NON_STRING with the three dropped values, so the invalid metadata is handled explicitly rather than silently filtered.

Defines the deterministic index-rendering contract reused for the normalized corpus index: entries are grouped by type in the fixed GROUP_ORDER (source, entity, concept, comparison, synthesis), items are sorted by title, and any unlisted type is emitted afterwards (L109-113), with 'index.md' and other structural files excluded. Task-relevant behavior: the demo renders out/wiki-index.md with the same ordering discipline, so the group order is Sources -> Entities -> Assets -> Other and page lists are sorted by path; no locale-dependent comparison is used.

Shows the real ingest pipeline normalizing a page's on-disk path: when frontmatter has both a usable type and title it returns 'wiki/${dirForType(type)}/${slugify(title)}.md' (L397-400), exactly the helper chain the demo imports; when they are missing it falls back to canonicalizing the declared path's directory segment (L402-410). Task-relevant behavior: this is why malformed frontmatter cannot make pages escape the canonical layout in the demo — the type fallback 'other' plus the basename title still yields a stable wiki/other/<basename>.md path.

Reference for heading-based splitting: L32 treats every line matching /^#{1,6}\s+\S/ as a heading boundary regardless of fenced code blocks. Task-relevant behavior: the demo reuses the same heading notion for its duplicate-heading census but makes it fence-aware, so indented comments such as '# Check the proxy logs for THIS sid:' (ops-notes.md) or '# 注意：...' (agent-codex.md) are counted as skipped-in-fence lines (1 each) instead of becoming phantom headings — a documented, deterministic refinement that keeps the anchor table stable.

claims.claim: Slug normalization is deterministic and idempotent: slugify() is a pure scan of the input string, so equal inputs always produce equal slugs and re-slugifying a slug is a no-op. Corpus evidence: 'Redis 主从' -> 'redis-主从', 'redis-主从!' -> 'redis-主从', '1. 客户端接入配置' -> '1-客户端接入配置'; the demo verifies slugify(slugify(x)) === slugify(x) over 27 corpus-derived probes and the failure of any probe fails the run.

Canonical page identity is deterministic: dirForType() + pageRelPath() turn (type, title) into 'wiki/<dir>/<slug>.md', which makes dedup reproducible. Corpus evidence: entity-redis-2.md ('redis-主从!') and entity-redis.md ('Redis 主从') request the same path wiki/entities/redis-主从.md; the demo detects the collision, keeps the first file (code-point file order) on the requested path and moves the second to wiki/entities/redis-主从-2.md, recording PAGE_PATH_COLLISION with the applied suffix. Unregistered type 'assets' and fallback type 'other' resolve to wiki/assets/ and wiki/other/ instead of failing.

Duplicate headings are re-anchored deterministically per normalized page (file-path order, then line order; first occurrence keeps the bare slug, later ones get -2/-3/...). Corpus evidence: 6 duplicates observed and resolved — '扫什么' -> '扫什么-2' (agent-codex.md:28), '集群模式！' -> '集群模式-2' (entity-redis-2.md:13, different raw text, same slug), '主从复制' -> '主从复制-2'/'主从复制-3' (entity-redis.md:5/:9 merged with entity-redis-2.md:5), 'Redis 主从' -> 'redis-主从-2', '1. 客户端接入配置' -> '1-客户端接入配置-2' (ops-notes.md:12); all anchors are unique per page and the same input always yields the same anchor table. Heading census is fence-aware, unlike the naive chunker regex.

Invalid frontmatter is handled explicitly, never silently and never fatally: 5 of 9 corpus files have a rejected block (unterminated, invalid-yaml, duplicate-key, not-mapping, absent) and each yields at least one error diagnostic naming the exact fallback, ending in type='other' with the file basename as title — matching the tolerant parseFrontmatter() contract. In addition, a valid block with invalid fields produces explicit field-level diagnostics: FM_TITLE_FALLBACK (missing title -> basename, the index-builder rule) and FM_SOURCES_NOT_ARRAY / FM_SOURCES_NON_STRING (mirroring readSources' string-only filter). 0 rejected files are silent and 0 end up with a type other than 'other'.

The normalized result is reproducible byte-for-byte across processes because the pipeline contains no volatile input: 3 fresh in-process runs of the whole corpus produce identical bytes, a second OS process reproduces the identical report (sha256 90c759a0f47b699b9401de971328b9880f3531f406fffbd23e107d500205861a, canonical state digest a0323e7f353bcc1d352d9a0fe13da9171507bcc060a78b210b3f8a834a7eb637) and out/wiki-index.md is rendered with the same ordered grouping discipline as renderIndex (no timestamps, no randomness, no locale-dependent comparison).

conclusion: The repository's slug contract transfers cleanly to a different corpus (the docs/agents documentation set) containing duplicate headings and malformed frontmatter. With the real, unmodified symbols slugify/dirForType/pageRelPath imported from MemoryKnowledge/src/engines/wiki/ingest-v2/slug.ts, all 9 corpus files normalize without throwing: 8 deterministic page paths (1 cross-file collision merged and suffixed -2), 6 duplicate headings resolved to unique deterministic anchors (-2/-3), and 5 files with rejected frontmatter plus 2 files with invalid fields each emitting an explicit diagnostic that records the exact fallback (type=other, basename title, filtered sources). Determinism is demonstrated, not asserted: slugify is idempotent over 27 probes, three fresh runs are byte-identical, and two separate processes write the identical report (sha256 90c759a0f47b699b9401de971328b9880f3531f406fffbd23e107d500205861a). The only unexecutable part of the chain is parseFrontmatter() itself, because its `yaml` dependency is absent and dependency installation is out of scope; that limitation is recorded in the report and in the validation notes, and the demo mirrors that contract while adding the explicitness the library omits.

LIMITATION (optional validation dependency unavailable): MemoryKnowledge/src/engines/wiki/ingest-v2/frontmatter.ts imports the `yaml` package, which is not installed in this workspace and must not be installed, so ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND prevents executing the real parseFrontmatter()/readSources().
